items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 has 6 number providers (EnchantmentLevelProvider, ScoreboardValue, StorageValue all in the server jar). Both Rust implementations handle only 3 (constant/uniform/binomial) — enchantment_level/score/storage fall to _ => 0 (loot.rs int/float 1346-1385; items.rs number 2033-2063). Data check: 0/1355 vanilla 26.2 loot tables use the 3 missing providers. The only enchantment_level uses in 26.2 datapack (soul_speed/thorns chance) go through the separate enchant.rs random_chance path, which handles it explicitly and matches vanilla's amount.calculate(level) exactly.
items.title: Three number providers return 0 (datapack-only) [= 1.21.7 B11-G12]

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 AnyFuel.resolve returns FuelValues.fuelItems() — the keySet of an insertion-ordered Object2IntLinkedOpenHashMap populated by the hardcoded vanillaBurnTimes sequence (LAVA_BUCKET first). The Rust groups fuels by burn-time value in registry order (recipe_book.rs:566-585, native_panel_recipes.rs:173-190) — first fuel in registry order is oak planks (id 63; lava bucket 1042). Burn times unaffected, display order only. 26.3-form carry-over: 26.3 resolves via DataComponentLookup.findAll(COOKING_FUEL).
items.title: Recipe-book fuel slot cycles fuels in the wrong order [= 1.21.7 B11-G15]

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.2 DebugEntrySoundMood appends String.format(ROOT, "  (Mood %d%%)") — TWO spaces — to the channel debug string. The Rust's sound_mood_line (debug_overlay.rs:399-408) uses ONE space: "Sounds: {}/{} + {}/{} (Mood {}%)". Cosmetic. The other two thirds of 1.21.7's B11-G20 do NOT apply: 26.2's Local Difficulty line has no Day suffix (day count is a separate DebugEntryDayCount entry, "Day #", which the Rust renders) and 26.2's memory lines use MiB, as does the Rust. 26.3's entry literal is also two-spaced, so this is a 26.1-form leftover, not a 26.3 leak.
items.title: F3 sound mood has one space before (Mood [part of 1.21.7 B11-G20]
